findings.title: Sign job unpacks the build job's tar over its own checkout, so code from the build job can replace scripts/sign.sh and read the signing certificate
findings.description: The split is meant to guarantee that dependency code never runs where the signing key is (AGENTS.md, release notes). But `sign` checks out scripts/sign.sh, then runs `tar -xzf app.tgz` in the same folder, then runs `scripts/sign.sh` with MAC_CERT_P12 and MAC_CERT_PASSWORD in its env. app.tgz is made by `build`, where every dependency's code and install scripts run. That code controls what goes into app.tgz, and bsdtar overwrites existing files by default.
findings.failure_scenario: A compromised dependency or allowed install script runs in `build` and adds `scripts/sign.sh` (or a second `Protoplasma-x-mac-arm64.zip`) to app.tgz next to Protoplasma.app. In `sign`, the tar replaces the checked-out sign.sh. The replaced script then runs with the .p12 and its password and can send them out. Anyone holding that certificate can sign updates that every installed copy accepts (sameSigner). Any planted extra zip also gets uploaded by the `Protoplasma-*-mac-arm64.zip` glob.
findings.evidence: Tested in a scratch folder (work2/fixes-ci-docs/tartest). The checked-out scripts/sign.sh said 'good'. An archive made with `tar -czf app.tgz -C build Protoplasma.app scripts` held a sign.sh that said 'evil'. After `tar -xzf ../app.tgz`, `cat scripts/sign.sh` printed 'evil'. The workflow runs `- run: tar -xzf app.tgz` and then `scripts/sign.sh Protoplasma.app` in the same workspace.
findings.suggested_fix: Refuse any entry that isn't the app, and unpack into its own folder: `if tar -tzf app.tgz | grep -qv '^Protoplasma\.app\(/\|$\)'; then echo 'unexpected files in app.tgz'; exit 1; fi; mkdir out && tar -xzf app.tgz -C out`. Then sign and ditto `out/Protoplasma.app`. Another option is to check out sign.sh with `path: src` and call `src/scripts/sign.sh`.

findings.title: The unsigned-app artifact is kept for 1 day, but the sign job waits for a reviewer
findings.description: `retention-days: 1` is set on the upload. HANDOFF and plan.md tell David to add himself as a required reviewer on the `release` environment, and a job can wait up to 30 days for that approval. If he approves more than a day later, the artifact has expired and `sign` fails. plan.md then says a failed release needs a new commit and a new version.
findings.failure_scenario: The tag is pushed in the evening and the sign job is approved the next evening. download-artifact fails with 'artifact not found'. Re-running only `sign` fails the same way. Following plan.md, David bumps to 0.7.1, although 'Re-run all jobs' would have rebuilt and released 0.7.0, since nothing was published.
findings.evidence: release.yml build step: `retention-days: 1`. sign job: `environment: release`. plan.md: 'If it fails, the fix needs a new commit and a new version (0.7.1)'. HANDOFF step 2: 'add yourself as a required reviewer'.
findings.suggested_fix: Use `retention-days: 7` or more. Also say in plan.md and HANDOFF that if `sign` fails before anything is published, 'Re-run all jobs' is enough.

findings.title: Move to a team: the 409's advice "Rename this one, then move it again" can never work
findings.description: moveSession sends `name: key`, where key = rec.key whenever the session has been renamed (rec.key !== slug(name)). A hub rename keeps the original key (`session.key = keyOf(session)`). So after the rename the 409 tells you to do, the move sends the same original key again. Hub findSession matches on slug, key and aliases, so it finds the same target session and answers 409 again. Renaming the target's session doesn't help either, because it keeps its key and gains an alias. The fix is also half-done for a session that was already renamed. The 409 check only covers `key`. If the target already has a session called `name`, saveSession creates `key` there, then renameSession(key -> name) answers 409. That leaves a stray session in the target, named after the key, and the source session is never marked done.
findings.failure_scenario: 1) Move "lobby" from Just me to Team B. Just me keeps its copy, marked done. 2) Move it back to Just me: the hub's findSession matches the done "lobby" and answers 409, "Rename this one, then move it again". 3) Rename it in B to "lobby2": rec.key stays "lobby", so moveSession again sends name "lobby" and gets 409. The same loop happens for any target that has an unrelated session called "lobby". The only way out is deleting the target's session, which the message doesn't mention. Release notes 0.7.0 line 67 repeats the advice that doesn't work.
findings.evidence: renderer.js moveSession: `const key = rec?.key && rec.key !== slug(name) ? rec.key : name; await proto.saveSession(target.key, { name: key, task, move: true })`. hub.js ~858: `const existed = findSession(team, name); if (existed && body.move === true) return json(409, ...)`. findSession matches `keyOf(x) === want || aliases`. The hub rename route sets `session.key = keyOf(session)` and pushes the old name into aliases.
findings.suggested_fix: Have the hub check both the key and the display name (or send both, e.g. `{name: key, as: name, move: true}`), and let the 409 name the real way out. For example, offer to move it under a new key: save under a fresh unique name, then rename. That needs the folder key passed separately, the way folderKey is already passed to startLane. Or tell the person to delete or rename the session on the other side and accept that the key is kept. Also make the key-then-rename pair atomic: check `name` before creating `key`.

findings.title: The cleanAgent fix (renderer-solo-5) leaves out lastActive, the field the review's own scenario used
findings.description: The new coercion forces name, login, cmd, status, branch, repo, tree and prompt to strings. lastActive still passes through unchanged. So do session records' createdAt and doneAt: the new sessions filter only checks that `name` is a string. sessionList builds `at` from l.lastActive, rec.doneAt and rec.createdAt, and renderSessions' default sort calls `b.at.localeCompare(a.at)`. The comment says the change stops a number from blanking the window, but this path still throws. The review's suggested fix named lastActive explicitly.
findings.failure_scenario: A hub on a Mac (hostile, buggy or older) sends one lane with `lastActive: 123`, or one session record with `createdAt: 1`, in a team with two or more sessions. renderSessions' sort throws 'b.at.localeCompare is not a function' on every state frame, and the window stays blank or stale while that team is open.
findings.evidence: diff: `['name','login','cmd','status','branch','repo','tree','prompt'].map(...)`, with no lastActive. renderer.js ~1215: `at: ls.map(l => l.lastActive).concat(rec?.doneAt || rec?.createdAt || '').filter(Boolean).sort().pop() || ''`. ~1252: `(a, b) => rank(a) - rank(b) || b.at.localeCompare(a.at)`. Review docs/sessions/2026-11-25-review.md:429 names this exact case: 'lastActive: 123 ... at.localeCompare is not a function'.
findings.suggested_fix: Add 'lastActive' (and 'typedBy') to the coerced keys, and force `at` to a string in sessionList (String(...) or a typeof filter). Alternatively coerce createdAt and doneAt when filtering m.sessions.

findings.title: movedOn checks names in localStorage only: stale keys hide the folder prompt for good, and a rename in the other team slips past it
findings.description: movedOn counts any `source:<other team>:<name>` key with the same repo. Your own key is cleared only when you delete the session yourself. So a key survives when a teammate deleted the session, when you left the team or it was deleted, and for the done copy a move leaves behind. After that, "Also remove its folder on this Mac?" is never offered again for that name and repo: the folder is kept with no prompt. It also misses the opposite case. The rename form moves the source key to the new name (renameForm copies sourceKey(old) to sourceKey(next)). Once the moved copy is renamed in the other team, `endsWith(':' + name)` no longer matches, and deleting the original offers to remove a folder that team still uses. Only main's new guard stops that, and only while an agent is running. `endsWith(':lobby')` also matches an unrelated session called "a:lobby".
findings.failure_scenario: Move "lobby" from Just me to Team B, then rename it in B to "lobby v2". Later, delete the done "lobby" in Just me while no agent runs in B. movedOn is false and the confirm appears. removeSessionFolder deletes <clone>@lobby, which B's session works in. The branch is kept and uncommitted or ignored work refuses the delete, so the loss is limited, but B's next agent has to recreate the worktree. In the other direction, after a teammate deletes a session in a team you share, your stale source key stops Just me's same-named session from ever offering to remove its folder.
findings.evidence: renderer.js 1048: `Object.keys(localStorage).some(k => k.startsWith('source:') && k !== sourceKey(name) && k.endsWith(`:${name}`) && JSON.parse(...).repo === source.repo)`. renameForm.onsubmit: `store.set(key(next), value); store.set(key(old), '')`. deleteSession clears only `sourceKey(name)` for the current team.
findings.suggested_fix: Make main the authority, since it already knows the folder. In sessions:removeFolder, or in a new check, refuse or skip when any live lane's cwd is under the folder (as now). For the prompt, match on the folder key rather than the display name: store the key in the source JSON and compare `source.key`/folder path. Accept the leak and note it with `ponytail:`.

findings.title: move:true is ignored by hubs running older code, which then silently join the same-named session
findings.description: Only the new hub returns the 409 for `move: true`. A team hosted on a teammate's Mac that runs 0.6.x ignores the field and joins the existing session of that name, which the fix exists to prevent. So does the online hub until it's redeployed. The renderer doesn't check the reply to see that a new record was created, so the move then marks the source done and opens someone else's session.
findings.failure_scenario: Max hosts a team on his Mac with 0.6.1 and already has a session "lobby". David (0.7.0) uses Move to a team on his own "lobby" into Max's team. Max's hub joins it. David's agents there work in his folder under Max's session (goal, plan, steps) and his Just me copy is marked done.
findings.evidence: hub.js 858: `if (existed && body.move === true) return json(409, ...)` exists only in the new code. renderer moveSession ignores the records that saveSession returns.
findings.suggested_fix: In moveSession, check the returned records before going on. The record named `key` should be new: its createdBy is me, and it wasn't in the target before. Otherwise stop and alert. Alternatively list the target's sessions first and refuse in the renderer.

findings.title: (Pre-existing, not from the fixes) the hub's session DELETE never refuses while agents are running
findings.description: The guard calls `running(session.name)`, but running is defined as `(team, x) => teamLanes(team.id).some(l => l.session === x.name)`. With one argument, team.id is undefined: teamLanes(undefined) matches no lane (every lane has a team id), and x is undefined but `.some` on an empty list never reads it. So the 409 'Stop its agents first.' can never fire.
findings.failure_scenario: The session's creator or the team owner deletes a session from another window or an older app while a teammate's agents are running in it. The hub removes it and its stopped-agent records. The running agents' terminals then show under a session with no record.
findings.evidence: hub.js 172: `const running = (team, x) => teamLanes(team.id).some(l => l.session === x.name)`. 316: `teamLanes = teamId => [...lanes.values()].filter(l => l.team === teamId)`. 888: `if (running(session.name)) return json(409, ...)`.
findings.suggested_fix: `if (running(team, session)) return json(409, { error: 'Stop its agents first.' });` and add an api() test in hub.test.js.

checked_and_sound: teams.js refuseOnce keyed on sha256(slim)+reason: slimHook keeps only hook_event_name, cwd, tool_name and tool_input.{file_path, notebook_path, cmd, command}, so no ids, timestamps, workdir or timeout reach the key. A byte-identical Codex or OpenCode retry gives the same key. Codex's and OpenCode's apply_patch are cut to the file-header lines, so retrying a patch on the same files matches even if its content changed. The lan.test.js case does test a different step with the same reason.
main.js sessions:save: the `...(o.move && { move: true })` pass-through is coerced to a boolean, and teams.saveSession forwards the body unchanged to the hub, which checks `body.move === true`.

main.js sessions:removeFolder guard: path is imported; lane.cwd comes from github.sessionFolder's dir, the same `<clone>@<slug>` as sessionFolderPath; a null dir (folder gone) can't match; exited lanes leave `lanes` in onExit; Delete session is disabled while the session's own agents run, so the guard only catches other teams' agents, as intended.

renderer cleanAgent: no render code uses `??` on the coerced fields, and the hub's views() sends every key, so turning a missing field into '' changes no fallback; `git` as null vs undefined is only used for truthiness (`l.git?.x`, `lanes.filter(l => l.git)`).
members via nameList: isSolo uses `t.members.length` and still works.
checkInvites busy/at: busy is reset in finally, early returns inside the try go through finally, the 10-minute interval is unaffected, and focus is limited to once a minute.
Just me invite confirm: there is only one proto.invite call site, isSolo becomes false once someone is invited, and sessionRecords belongs to the team being invited into.

New session: typedTask (up to 12000) goes to the first prompt, the same as main's firstPrompt cap; the goal is sliced to the hub's 300; sessionNameFrom cuts the name to 5 words and 40 characters; the session name input stays at maxlength 60.

defaultAgent: agents:status always returns a boolean `installed` (including the Other entry); with an empty list it returns prefs.agent, as before; a cleared Other command now falls back to an installed agent.
No new top-level names in renderer.js that clash with code.js or panes.js (movedOn and typedTask are local; checkInvites.busy/.at are function properties).

findings.title: send() now terminates a window that is only receiving one burst of screen replays, which causes a reconnect loop
findings.description: send() checks bufferedAmount > MAX_BUFFERED (16 MB) before every message. The `look` handler (line ~1108) and the no-`sees` connect path (line ~1091) call send() in a synchronous loop, one `out` per lane, each carrying up to 512K chars of history. Nothing drains between iterations, so bufferedAmount ends up as the size of the whole burst minus the kernel buffer, however fast the client reads. Once that passes 16 MB the socket is terminated with 1006 and every queued byte is thrown away. The window never got its screens. Before the fix these sends went through. toTeam's identical check is harmless because live output arrives in small 16 ms batches.
findings.failure_scenario: A team has roughly 15 to 25 busy agents across the sessions one window shows (up to 8, e.g. pane mode with 3 sessions). The window sends `look`, the hub queues more than 16 MB in one tick and terminates the socket. The renderer reconnects and sends the same `look`, and the hub terminates it again. Those terminals never fill, and the hub serialises about 20 MB on every round.
findings.evidence: Repro at scratchpad/work2/fixes-hub-lane/probe2.js: a hub on 127.0.0.1 with 20 lanes in session 's', each with about 506K chars of escape-heavy history, and a normally reading watcher that sends look {sees:['s']}. Result: `WATCHER CLOSED code 1006 after outs 0`, peak server-side bufferedAmount 17.3 MB. With 16 lanes the watcher stays open (peak 16.2 MB). Code: `const send = (ws, msg) => ws.readyState === ws.OPEN && (ws.bufferedAmount > MAX_BUFFERED ? ws.terminate() : ws.send(JSON.stringify(msg)));` and `if (!viewing()) for (const l of teamLanes(team.id)) if (sees.has(l.session) && !ws.sees.has(l.session)) send(ws, { t: 'out', ... d: `\x1bc${l.history}` });`
findings.suggested_fix: Apply the drop to sockets that have stopped reading, not to one burst: check the threshold once before the replay loop (or in a separate sendOrDrop used only for single messages), and once over the limit skip the remaining replays (those terminals start from the next output) instead of terminating.

findings.title: The new push-redirect forms are missed once quoted, and an alias set for later skips the push check entirely
findings.description: wordsOf strips quotes only at a word's two ends. `GIT_CONFIG_KEY_0="remote.origin.push"` therefore becomes `GIT_CONFIG_KEY_0="remote.origin.push`, setting() slices after '=' and gets `"remote.origin.push`, and the anchored PUSH_CONFIG (^remote\.) doesn't match it. `--config-env="remote.origin.push=T"` fails the same way. The fix also covers `-c alias.x=...push` but not the same alias set with `git config alias.x ...`. After that, `git x` isn't read as a push at all. Other redirects of the kind the test treats as one (pushurl) are also missed: url.*.pushInsteadOf, remote.pushDefault, branch.*.pushRemote and GIT_CONFIG_PARAMETERS.
findings.failure_scenario: On a team with members, an agent on session/fix runs `git config alias.ship "push --force origin HEAD:main" && git ship`, or `GIT_CONFIG_COUNT=1 GIT_CONFIG_KEY_0="remote.origin.push" GIT_CONFIG_VALUE_0="HEAD:main" git push`. Main is pushed (force-pushed in the first case) with no ask.
findings.evidence: scratchpad/work2/fixes-hub-lane/push.js (hub on 127.0.0.1, a team with a member, a lane on session/fix, PreToolUse Bash hooks): every one of these answers no decision: the quoted KEY_0 form, `git --config-env="remote.origin.push=T" push`, the alias form, `git config url.git@evil:x/.pushInsteadOf ...`, `git config remote.pushDefault evil`, and the GIT_CONFIG_PARAMETERS form. The unquoted KEY_0 form answers `ask`.
findings.suggested_fix: In setting(), strip quotes from the result (`.replace(/["']/g, '')`) before testing. Add `alias\..+` (when its value contains push), `url\..+\.(push)?insteadof`, `remote\.pushdefault` and `branch\..+\.pushremote` to the keys that ask. Treat a `GIT_CONFIG_PARAMETERS=` word that contains a PUSH_CONFIG key as a redirect. Add the quoted forms to hub.test.js.

findings.title: The move 409 says to rename the session, which can never clear it, and moving a session back is now impossible
findings.description: moveSession sends `name: key`, the session's first slug, which stays the same across renames so the folder and branch don't move. Hub findSession matches `keyOf(x) === slug(name)` and aliases, and a rename keeps both the key and the old name as an alias. So after the advised rename, on either side, the same 409 comes back. Moving a session back to the team it came from always hits its own old done record, which moveSession leaves behind. Before the fix that move joined that record, which in this case was correct.
findings.failure_scenario: Move 'fix-login' from Just me to Team X. Just me keeps a done 'fix-login'. Later, Move to Just me from Team X gets 409 'That team already has a session called "fix-login". Rename this one, then move it again.' The person renames it in Team X to 'fix-login 2' and moves again. The renderer still sends name 'fix-login' (rec.key), so it gets 409 again. The only way out is deleting the old record.
findings.evidence: renderer moveSession: `const key = rec?.key && rec.key !== slug(name) ? rec.key : name; await proto.saveSession(target.key, { name: key, ..., move: true })`. Hub: `if (existed && body.move === true) return json(409, ...)`, where findSession matches `slug(x.name) === want || keyOf(x) === want || aliases`.
findings.suggested_fix: Let a move join a record that is the same session: done, the same key, and created by the mover (or the source record the renderer names). Otherwise word the 409 without suggesting a rename, e.g. 'delete or rename the one there first', since only the target-side record can be changed to clear it.

findings.title: The merge-tree quarantine adds a synchronous git spawn in Electron's main process, and the landed check is recomputed on every HEAD move
findings.description: quarantined() calls the synchronous git() (execFileSync) for `rev-parse --git-path objects` on every mergeTree or mergedTree. lane.js runs inside the app's main process, so each call blocks it briefly. branchConflicts recomputes whenever HEAD, the branch or main moves. Each own commit therefore re-runs up to 10 branches × (mergedTree + mergeTree): up to 20 sync spawns, each with its own mkdtemp/rm, per agent. Yet mergedTree(main, at) and main^{tree} don't depend on HEAD.
findings.failure_scenario: Several agents commit often in a repo with 10 pushed session branches. Each commit runs about 20 extra sync git spawns and twice the merge-trees, which shows up as small main-process stalls. Each spawn is cheap (under 10 ms measured here), so the cost is mostly wasted work.
findings.evidence: `const objects = path.resolve(cwd, git(cwd, 'rev-parse', '--git-path', 'objects') || '.git/objects');` inside quarantined. `const landed = own && await mergedTree(cwd, main, at, env) === await line('rev-parse', `${main}^{tree}`);` inside the per-branch block keyed on `${head}\n${at}\n${mainAt}`.
findings.suggested_fix: Cache the objects path per cwd (it never changes) or get it with the async line(), and cache `landed` by `${at}\n${mainAt}`.

findings.title: OpenCode subagents no longer get team context
findings.description: chat.message now returns early for child sessions, so a subagent's requests never get UserPromptSubmit's additionalContext: session goal, plan, other agents and their files, and the behind warning. A subagent that edits files works without knowing a teammate changed them. Only the refuse-once PreToolUse answer is left. The child's context entry is also never reset, because context.delete is skipped, so notes from its tool calls pile up for the child's whole life.
findings.failure_scenario: An OpenCode agent hands an edit to its `general` subagent through the task tool. The subagent's system prompt has none of the team context, so it edits a file a teammate is changing. Its first edit is refused once and the retry goes through, never having seen the overlap warning the main session would have got.
findings.evidence: `'chat.message': async ({ sessionID } = {}, { parts } = {}) => { if (children.has(sessionID)) return; context.delete(sessionID); ... tell(sessionID, (await post({ hook_event_name: 'UserPromptSubmit', prompt })).additionalContext); }`
findings.suggested_fix: For children, still ask for the context but flag the request (e.g. `subagent: true`) so the hub doesn't record it as the person's prompt or change the lane's status. Or copy the parent session's current context into the child when session.created arrives with a parentID.

checked_and_sound: merge-tree quarantine works with a linked worktree of a `git clone --shared` repo: objects are read through GIT_ALTERNATE_OBJECT_DIRECTORIES, the repo's own info/alternates is followed, the conflict is still found, the loose-object count is unchanged and no protoplasma-merge-* temp dir is left (scratchpad/work2/fixes-hub-lane/alt)
quarantined() removes its temp dir in finally. The execFile callbacks always resolve (timeouts included), so no rejection skips the cleanup
The landed check (mergedTree(main, branch) === main^{tree}) is correct for squash and rebase merges. Operator precedence: `own && ((await a) === (await b))`
conflicts.test.js's 'no objects left behind' check would fail on the old code: HEAD moves, so mainConflicts and branchConflicts both re-run merge-tree

send() terminating cannot throw. On lanes (`in`) and on the file relay (one message up to 1M chars) the 16 MB check is effectively never reached. Later sends to a terminated socket are skipped because readyState isn't OPEN
claimsOn returns three and leaves the 4th and later untold for the next edit of that file. The hub-live test checks 3 then 1
mentions() without includes() no longer matches a.ts inside data.ts. A full path still matches through its '/name' boundary
The `move` flag passes through main.js (`...(o.move && { move: true })`) and teams.js saveSession to the hub
CLIENT_ID is a constant (not read from env at load), so the identity test comparing it with config.json githubClientId is stable
Dropping the --show-origin/-l exemption causes no false positive for `git config -l`, `--list --show-origin` or `--show-origin --get ...`

verdicts.reasoning: release.yml lines 72-88: `sign` does a sparse checkout of scripts/sign.sh and docs/release-notes. It then downloads app.tgz into the same workspace and runs `tar -xzf app.tgz` (line 82) there. After that it runs `scripts/sign.sh Protoplasma.app` with MAC_CERT_P12 and MAC_CERT_PASSWORD in its env. app.tgz comes from `build`, where npm ci, the allowed install scripts, the tests and the packager all run, so dependency code controls what goes into the tar. I reproduced it in work2/verify-fixes-ci-docs/t: an archive holding Protoplasma.app plus scripts/sign.sh ('evil'), unpacked over a workspace whose scripts/sign.sh said 'good', leaves 'evil' in place. bsdtar overwrites by default. sign.sh writes the decoded .p12 to a temp folder and uses the password, so a replaced script gets both. Nothing else checks what the archive contains. An extra Protoplasma-*-mac-arm64.zip in the tar would also be picked up by the gh release glob. So the split's stated guarantee (dependency code never runs where the signing key is) does not hold. A compromised build could already ship a malicious app that then gets signed. Stealing the certificate adds lasting control on top of that, because sameSigner trusts every later update signed with it.
verdicts.fix_notes: Before unpacking, refuse any entry outside Protoplasma.app: `tar -tzf app.tgz | grep -qv '^Protoplasma\.app\(/\|$\)' && { echo 'unexpected files in app.tgz'; exit 1; }`. Then unpack into its own folder (`mkdir out && tar -xzf app.tgz -C out`), and sign and ditto `out/Protoplasma.app`. A further option is to check out sign.sh with `path: src` and call `src/scripts/sign.sh`.
